svg.aria-label: How to write ش ک ر: 3 letters, ش, ک, ر, one after another
svg.title: Writing ش ک ر
svg.desc: 3 letters written one after another: ش, ک, ر (urdu-nastaliq). Each letter has its own group of frames; frame N of a group shows movements 1 to N of that letter, the movement being added drawn in ink over the finished letter, whose outline is read from _fonts/NotoNaskhArabic-Static.ttf. Each letter is drawn at its own scale from its own cited stroke order, so the strip does not show how large the letters are next to each other, how far apart they sit, or any join between them. Stroke order: ش: Zer o Zabar, Sīn, shīn, baṛī he, nūn, and nūn-e ġhunna, independent ش calligraphic and handwriting animations and Shīn instructions (Northwestern University Libraries Open Textbook, 2026) <https://openbooks.library.northwestern.edu/zerozabar/chapter/sin-shin-bari-he-nun-nun-ghunna/>; ک: Zer o Zabar, Be, kāf, and short vowels, independent ک calligraphic and handwriting animations and Kāf instructions (Northwestern University Libraries Open Textbook, 2026) <https://openbooks.library.northwestern.edu/zerozabar/chapter/be-kaf-and-short-vowels/>; ر: Zer o Zabar, Dāl, re, and wāw, independent ر handwriting animation and Re instructions (Northwestern University Libraries Open Textbook, 2026) <https://openbooks.library.northwestern.edu/zerozabar/chapter/dal-re-and-waw/>. Source notes on variation: ش: The independent-form animations draw the full standard toothed sīn body first in one uninterrupted stroke, then place the lower-left dot, the lower-right dot, and finally the centered upper dot: four strokes separated by three pen lifts. The lesson arranges the dots as two below with one nestled between them above. As with sīn, an optional long gentle curve may replace the teeth, especially in handwriting, while the three dots stay centered over either form. This learner path covers the standard toothed independent form and fits the course's vendored Noto Naskh fallback; Urdu is conventionally printed in Nastaliq, and the app's true Nastaliq face remains separate from this canonical script-data fallback. ک: Both independent-form animations and the adjacent prose show two separate pen strokes. First draw the stem as part of the main line, continuing right to left through the flatter bowl and pronounced final hook without lifting. Then lift once, return to the upper right, and draw the long downward slash toward the stem; the lesson explicitly says not to write kāf in one penstroke. Final and independent kāf are often flatter than be and have a more pronounced hook at the end. This learner path fits that order to the course's vendored Noto Naskh fallback; Urdu uses ک rather than Arabic ك, is conventionally printed in Nastaliq, and the app's true Nastaliq face remains separate from this canonical script-data fallback. ر: The independent-form animation and adjacent prose show one uninterrupted stroke: draw a downward line, then curve to the left. The final form instead drops sharply to the lower left from the preceding letter. The lesson also notes that final re rises in Naskh but not in Nastaliq. This learner path covers the independent form and fits the course's vendored Noto Naskh fallback; Urdu is conventionally printed in Nastaliq, and the app's true Nastaliq face remains separate from this canonical script-data fallback.
svg.text: How it is written — 3 letters, one after another
Letter 1 of 3 — 4 strokes · 3 pen lifts · 5 movements
Letter 2 of 3 — 2 strokes · 1 pen lift · 3 movements
Letter 3 of 3 — one unbroken stroke · 2 movements
Letter 1: stroke order after Zer o Zabar, Sīn, shīn, baṛī he, nūn, and nūn-e ġhunna, independent ش calligraphic and handwriting animations and Shīn
Letter 2: stroke order after Zer o Zabar, Be, kāf, and short vowels, independent ک calligraphic and handwriting animations and Kāf instructions
Letter 3: stroke order after Zer o Zabar, Dāl, re, and wāw, independent ر handwriting animation and Re instructions (Northwestern University Libraries Open
This order is attested, not standardised; the source records where it varies.
